capabilities: Sync the whole vault, including the config folder, plugins, and themes, across desktop and mobile devices
Encrypt file contents, names, and paths on-device before upload with per-device Ed25519 keys
Approve, list by fingerprint, and revoke device keys, and create a recovery key
Merge edits to different parts of a note automatically and keep both versions when the same lines conflict
Restore past file versions from 30-day server history and run remote-only devices with encrypted-at-rest placeholders
disambiguation: Not a standalone encryption tool; it is a full sync system that does nothing without its own self-hosted server.
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.13 or later; encryption keys are kept in Obsidian's secret storage. Release files carry GitHub build provenance attestations. Beta versions are distributed via BRAT with a data-loss warning. Detailed documentation lives in the repository's docs/ folder (self-hosting, crypto, protocol, API).
motivation: The README positions it as the simplest way to securely sync a vault and own your data, with a server that stores only ciphertext.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to sync a vault through a server you own where contents, file names, and folder paths stay encrypted from the server.

relations.evidence: To try one, install BRAT and add the beta plugin ibehren1/obsidian-vault-syncryption-beta.

requires.name: Vault Syncryption self-hosted server (Docker host with public IP, DNS, ports 80/443)
Server account created with the admin's shared secret

summary: Self-hosted, end-to-end encrypted vault sync with device key approval, automatic conflict merging, file history, and remote-only devices.
